summary: LUNARITHM is an interactive lunar exploration prototype developed for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. It focuses on helping users explore selected lunar South Pole regions through a unified interface that presents geographic locations and their coordinates. The project aims to make early-stage lunar landing site exploration more accessible by organizing relevant location information in an interactive environment. Built using React and Vite for the frontend and Python FastAPI for the backend, LUNARITHM demonstrates how web technologies can support lunar exploration research and visualization. Its goal is to provide a foundation for understanding lunar terrain and supporting future landing-site analysis.
details:
LUNARITHM – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

Tagline: Decoding Lunar Terrain. Engineering Safer Landings.

LUNARITHM is a lunar landing-site analysis and decision-support platform designed to help identify and evaluate potential landing regions near the lunar South Pole. Future lunar missions face several challenges, including uneven terrain, extreme illumination conditions, limited visibility and communication constraints. Selecting a suitable landing region requires careful analysis of multiple scientific and environmental factors.

Our project addresses this challenge through an interactive web-based platform that combines lunar location data, scientific datasets and visual analysis to support informed landing-site assessment.

The prototype provides an interactive lunar South Pole map with three candidate regions: Malapert Massif, Nobile Rim 1 and de Gerlache Rim 2. Users can select locations, examine their coordinates and explore available illumination information. The backend processes the lunar illumination dataset and provides relevant coverage metrics and source information to the frontend. This helps users understand the environmental characteristics of candidate regions through a centralized interface.

The project uses NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) / Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Wide Angle Camera (WAC) south-pole illumination dataset at 100-metre spatial resolution. This scientific data provides an important basis for examining illumination conditions in the lunar polar region.

Technologies and Tools Used:

  • Frontend: React.js, Vite and CSS
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • Data communication: Axios and REST APIs
  • Mapping and visualization: Leaflet, React-Leaflet and Recharts
  • Icons and interface elements: Lucide React
  • Scientific data and resources: NASA LRO/LROC WAC datasets and NASA/JPL Horizons

Creativity and Innovation:

The key innovation of LUNARITHM is bringing lunar scientific information and candidate landing-region exploration together in an accessible, interactive decision-support interface. Instead of relying only on static maps or disconnected datasets, the platform provides location-based exploration and visual representation of available scientific information. Its modular architecture also allows additional environmental and mission-planning analysis capabilities to be incorporated.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

LUNARITHM aims to support preliminary lunar landing-site research by making scientific information easier to explore and interpret. It can help students, researchers and space enthusiasts understand the challenges involved in lunar site selection and support early-stage comparisons of potential landing regions. In the long term, the platform could be extended to incorporate terrain hazards, solar illumination analysis, Earth visibility, communication geometry and multi-factor site assessment.

During development, our team considered scientific data reliability, spatial resolution, candidate-location coordinates, usability, visualization clarity, modular development and the limitations of available datasets. We designed the platform as a scientific decision-support tool rather than an autonomous landing-control system.

LUNARITHM aims to contribute to safer and more informed lunar exploration by transforming complex lunar information into an accessible platform for preliminary landing-site assessment.
